> **Session focus:** *Questioning frameworks and integrated practice across ASCCR and POWER*

## Learning Objectives

* Use questioning frameworks to elicit goals, constraints, and assumptions
* Integrate ASCCR and POWER in complete practice consultations
* Translate verbal consultations into clear written documentation
* Consolidate skills across both blocks into a repeatable practice routine

## Description of Activities

On 21 May (Block 1), the day emphasized asking great questions (scope, outcomes, estimand, constraints) and practicing full consultations with peer feedback. We translated consultations into written documentation to capture decisions, assumptions, and next steps.

## Reflection (Gibbs Reflective Cycle)

### 1. Description

We practiced questioning as the engine of collaboration—clarifying purpose, success criteria, data realities, and constraints—then ran complete consultations with peer feedback. We converted conversations into written summaries that make decisions auditable.

### 2. Feelings

Initially I felt stretched—balancing deep listening with structured probing. As the day progressed, the flow improved: questions scaffolded empathy and rigor at the same time. Writing the summaries sharpened thinking.

### 3. Evaluation

The question sets reduced rework by exposing hidden assumptions early. Integrated practice surfaced small but costly habits (vague action items, missing timelines). Documentation locked in shared understanding and facilitated next steps.

### 4. Analysis

ASCCR highlights that strong Content emerges from shared framing; questioning is how we co-create that frame. Kolb’s cycle explains the benefit of immediate reflection and revision. Double-loop learning challenged my bias to “answer quickly”; better questions improved both efficiency and trust.

### 5. Conclusion

Great consulting is great questioning tied to disciplined follow-through. When questions align purpose, estimand, and design, downstream analyses and writing become smoother and more defensible.

### 6. Action Plan

I will maintain a questioning script (objectives, estimand, outcomes, design, constraints), an action-item template with owners/dates, and a one-page consultation summary format. I’ll schedule a monthly peer review of my consultation notes for calibration.
